labelChirho: pupil of the eye (apple of the eye)
descriptionChirho: The diminutive noun 'ishon' meaning 'little man' or 'pupil of the eye,' used figuratively in the phrase 'apple of the eye' to denote something precious and carefully guarded (Deut 32:10, Ps 17:8, Prov 7:2). Translations consistently render it as a body-part simile: spa: como–pupila–de, arb: كَحَدَقَةِ, kor: 눈동자–처럼, swa: kama–mboni–ya, hin: पुतली–की–तरह. This is the literal anatomical/figurative-precious sense.

The extended meaning of 'ishon' referring to the darkest part or the 'pupil' of the night — i.e., the blackest hour of deep darkness (Prov 7:9, Job 24:15). Multilingual evidence uniformly shifts from the eye metaphor to a temporal-darkness frame: eng: in–blackest / in–the–blackness–of, spa: en–lo–oscuro–de / en–oscuridad–de, arb: فِي–سَوَادِ, hin: अंधकार–में / अंधेरे–में, swa: katika–giza / katika–giza–la. This darkness-of-night sense is semantically distinct from the pupil-of-eye sense.
